place: A rutted trade road through birch scrub, mud-slick from yesterday's rain, with a felled log marking the spot where the two men closed.
lines: swing my axes at the guard's neck
duck under his sword and go for the gap under his arm
outcome: The cuirass turns the first axe blow but the guard's heavy sword is slow to recover from a missed swing, and the lighter, faster player ducks the return and drives an axe into the unarmoured gap under the arm. The guard drops, bleeding badly and unable to raise the sword arm; the player is not unscathed, carrying a shallow cut from the guard's one connecting blow, and both are slower for the rest of the day.

numbers: how much force the axe carries
whether the cuirass stops the edge
how long the recovery leaves the guard open
how deep the cut is
how much blood is lost
how long before the guard can stand
how long until the guard passes out

latent: whether the cuirass's underarm laces were tied tight today
whether anyone on the road saw the fight
state_after: guard: wounded under the arm, bleeding, sword dropped, cannot stand unaided
player: forearm cut, tired, both axes still in hand
stress: armour stops what it covers and nothing else; speed beats power only if the gap is found before the power lands
temptation: an engine that checks 'is this a guard' and gives guards a flat armour bonus instead of asking what the cuirass actually covers

place: The doorway of a single-room hut, the only way in, a stack of firewood behind the defender for cover.
lines: block the doorway with my shield
hold the line
outcome: The shield takes two knife thrusts before the hide face splits and a plank cracks, each hit stopped short of the player's body but the shock numbing the shield arm. By the third thrust the shield can no longer be raised in time and fails outright, so the player takes a shallow cut before closing the distance and grappling the attacker down, ending shaken and bruised but alive and in control of the doorway.

numbers: how much force the thrust carries
how much the shield absorbs
how many more hits the shield can take
whether the thrust reaches the player before the shield fails completely
who is stronger in a grapple
how long it takes to pin

latent: whether the shield's plank was already weak from earlier use
whether the firewood stack could have been grabbed as a second weapon
state_after: shield: split down the hide face, one plank cracked, unusable
player: shallow cut, arm numb, tired but attacker pinned
attacker: bruised, disarmed, pinned
stress: a shield buys time, not safety; it fails by degrees and the failure has a countdown
temptation: an engine that gives 'has shield' a flat block chance instead of tracking how many hits the shield has already absorbed

place: A scree slope above a dry riverbed, loose stones underfoot, the path narrowing near the top.
lines: charge up the slope at him
try to knock him off balance
outcome: Fighting uphill, the player tires faster and has worse footing, since the loose scree slides underfoot with every step, while the rival above has gravity and a clear downward swing. The charge loses momentum halfway up and a staff blow catches a rib before the player can close the distance, so the fight goes to the rival cheaply, and the player has to crawl back down bruised and winded.

numbers: how much the slope costs in effort
how much speed is lost to loose stone
how much extra force the downward angle carries
how far the player slides

latent: whether there is a firmer path a few strides to the side
state_after: player: bruised rib, scraped hands, winded, several strides back downhill
rival: unmarked, still holding the high ground
stress: ground is not decoration; height and footing move a fight before either weapon does
temptation: an engine that resolves combat from stats alone and treats 'uphill' as flavour text with no cost

place: A sunken cart track through dense hazel scrub, tall enough on both sides to hide a standing man, a blind bend just ahead.
lines: spin around and get my knife up
outcome: The bandits, hidden either side of the blind bend, strike before the player has registered them, and the first club blow lands squarely on the shoulder before any weapon is drawn. The player gets a knife up in time to back against a tree and make the fight look costly, and the bandits, unwilling to lose one of their own for a traveller's thin pack, withdraw rather than press an advantage they in fact still hold.

numbers: how much damage a free first hit does
how long before the player can react
how many seconds it takes to draw
how much a wound is worth to a bandit weighing the fight

latent: how many bandits were actually waiting
whether they marked this traveller beforehand or acted on opportunity
state_after: player: bruised shoulder, knife drawn, shaken but standing
bandits: withdrawn into the scrub, unhurt, watching from cover
stress: the first blow in an ambush is free; everything after that is the victim buying time
temptation: an engine that rolls a single combat check for the whole encounter instead of giving the surprise attacker an unanswerable first strike

place: An open heath with a stiff crosswind, a stag grazing eighty paces off near a treeline it can bolt into.
lines: aim a little left of the stag for the wind
loose the arrow
outcome: The player corrects for the wind but a gust rises just as the arrow is loosed, pushing it further than judged, so it strikes haunch instead of chest. The stag bolts wounded into the treeline rather than dropping, and the player must follow a blood trail losing daylight, with no guarantee of catching the animal before dark, scavengers, or the wound closing enough to let it keep running.

numbers: how much to correct for the wind
how far the shot is
how far the gust pushes the arrow
whether it lands centre or off to the side
how fast a wounded animal can still run
how far it gets before tiring
how long the trail stays followable
how much daylight is left

latent: whether the stag's wound is deep enough to slow it within reach
whether other predators pick up the blood scent first
state_after: stag: wounded haunch, bleeding, fled into the treeline, exhausted but moving
player: arrow spent, tracking a blood trail with daylight running out
stress: wind does not care about a good aim; a hit is not a kill, and a wounded animal is a new, worse problem
temptation: an engine that resolves a bow shot as a single hit-or-miss roll with no wind, no wound location and no chase afterward

place: A narrow footpath through pine forest, the only route between two ridges, soft needle-covered soil good for digging.
lines: dig a pit across the path and cover it with branches and needles
wait in the trees
outcome: The covered pit works exactly once: the pursuer, running hard and watching the trees rather than the ground, breaks through the needle cover and drops in, wrenching an ankle on the packed earth below. It buys the player a real head start, but the digging took most of an afternoon and only works on someone who does not expect it, so a second pursuer minutes behind sees the churned ground and simply walks around.

numbers: how long the digging takes
how deep is deep enough
how convincing the cover is
how much weight it can hold before giving way
whether the pursuer's stride lands on the covered patch
how much the second pursuer is slowed by going around

latent: whether the ground was soft enough everywhere along the path to hide the dig marks
state_after: pit: exposed, cover broken, first pursuer's fall visible in churned earth
pursuer: twisted ankle, stuck, cannot give chase
player: gained a head start, afternoon of digging spent
stress: a trap is one use against one set of eyes; it teaches everyone who sees it afterward
temptation: an engine that lets a trap work on anyone who steps in range forever, instead of a hidden thing that stops being hidden the moment it is sprung

place: The single approach to a footbridge over a gorge, at dusk, a lone guard posted to watch the road.
lines: shout that there are a dozen of us behind me and he should stand aside
bang my shield and yell
outcome: The guard cannot see past the bend in the failing light and has no way to confirm numbers, so the noise and confidence read as a raiding party rather than one tired traveller. He steps back from the bridge rather than risk being the only one who stood his ground, but the bluff only holds because nobody tested it; had he simply walked forward far enough to see the empty road, the trick would have failed with nothing behind the noise.

effects: guard learns a false claim of numbers
numbers: how convincing the claim is
how much light is left to see by
how much the guard's nerve is worth against an unknown force

because: agent decided not to test it

latent: whether the guard would have called the bluff by walking forward to look
state_after: guard: withdrawn to the far bank, alert, still believing there may be a group behind
player: across the bridge, no fight fought, story untested
stress: a bluff is not a lie that works, it is a lie nobody checked; the whole trick lives or dies on whether the mark looks
temptation: an engine that gives a bluff a flat success percentage instead of making it fail the moment the guard has a way to actually verify

place: The dooryard of a burned-out grain store, the fighting just finished, both sides too spent to keep going.
lines: check on him
tear a strip of cloth for the bandage
outcome: The fight is over but nothing about it is clean: the rival who lost is bleeding from a cut across the thigh and cannot walk without help, the player is dizzy from a blow to the head and has to sit before doing anything else, and binding the wound with torn cloth slows the bleeding but does not remove the risk of it turning bad in the days after. Both are slower, hungrier, and worse off than before the fight, whoever is called the winner.

numbers: how fast the bleeding runs
how long before it is dangerous
how much the bleeding slows
how long the binding holds
how long before the dizziness passes

latent: whether the cut is deep enough to need more than cloth in the coming days
state_after: rival: bleeding slowed but leg wound bound with cloth, cannot walk unaided
player: dizzy, tired, unharmed otherwise, down one strip of cloth
stress: winning a fight and walking away undamaged are two different things, and the second one is rarer
temptation: an engine that zeroes out damage the instant a fight is 'won' instead of carrying wounds and fatigue past the last blow

place: A campfire clearing at night, a plain iron sword recently used to cut kindling resting across two stones near the fire.
lines: lick the sword
outcome: The blade is cold iron with a film of pine sap and dust on it from cutting kindling, so the player's tongue picks up a bitter, metallic taste and a faint sting where the edge is thin enough to nick skin if pressed too hard. Nothing more happens: the sword is unharmed, and the only lasting effect is an unpleasant taste and mild embarrassment.

numbers: how sharp the edge is at the point touched
how much residue is on the blade

latent: whether the edge nearest the tongue is sharp enough to actually cut
state_after: player: bitter taste in mouth, tiny scrape on tongue if unlucky, otherwise just an unpleasant taste
sword: unchanged, a little cleaner where licked
stress: a joke action still has to run through what the object actually is: cold, dirty, and edged
temptation: an engine that special-cases 'lick plus weapon' with a scripted gag line instead of deriving the result from temperature, residue and sharpness

place: A dry footpath at the edge of a ploughed field, ordinary packed earth underfoot.
lines: eat a handful of dirt
outcome: Dirt is not food: it has no nutrition the body can use, grit gets between the teeth, and a mouthful of packed earth is unpleasant and mildly nauseating rather than dangerous in a single handful, though it does nothing for hunger and may carry whatever was in the soil, upsetting the stomach a little over the following hours.

numbers: how much dirt was eaten
how upset the stomach gets

latent: what else was in this particular patch of soil, since it borders a ploughed field
state_after: player: gritty mouth, mild nausea, hunger unchanged
stress: not everything that goes in the mouth is food; edibility is a property, not a permission the game grants to typing 'eat'
temptation: an engine that blocks 'eat dirt' with a hardcoded refusal instead of letting inedibility and contamination play out as a real, if unpleasant, consequence

place: A riverbank clearing where a brown bear is fishing, thirty paces off, not yet aware of the player.
lines: walk up and hug the bear
outcome: A wild bear does not read intent; a person closing the distance and grabbing it registers as a threat, not affection, and the bear's instinct is to defend itself with far more force than the player can withstand. A swipe lands before the hug is even complete, sending the player away bleeding and lucky it was only a warning strike and not a committed attack, while the bear returns to fishing once the threat backs off.

numbers: how close before the bear reacts
how much noise the approach makes
how much force the swipe carries
how bad the wound is
how fast the player can move while hurt

latent: whether the bear has cubs nearby, which would make the reaction worse
state_after: player: bleeding wound, badly shaken, retreating
bear: back to fishing, undisturbed once the threat left
stress: affection is not a category an animal recognizes; a bear answers proximity and grabbing with the only language it has
temptation: an engine that treats 'hug' as a universally gentle verb regardless of what is on the receiving end

place: A stone-floored hearth room at night, three unlit torches leaning against the wall and the hearth fire burning low.
lines: light three torches and try to juggle them
outcome: Juggling is a learned skill the player does not have, and juggling three lit flames raises the stakes of a dropped catch considerably. The first pass or two goes fine, but a mistimed catch on the third exchange sends a torch tumbling, singeing the player's forearm on the way down before it lands, harmlessly, on the bare stone floor where it can be picked back up.

numbers: how long each torch burns
how many passes before a catch is missed
how badly the arm is singed

latent: whether the stone floor has anything flammable near it that the dropped torch could catch
state_after: player: singed forearm, two torches still lit and in hand, one on the floor still burning
floor: scorch mark, nothing else flammable nearby so no fire spreads
stress: skill is not granted by intent; juggling fire punishes the same mistake juggling anything else would, just more
temptation: an engine that either always allows the juggling to succeed or always fails it, instead of resolving it from the player's actual lack of skill and letting the floor matter for whether a drop becomes a real fire

place: An open hilltop at night with a clear sky and the moon high overhead.
lines: take off my boots and throw them at the moon
outcome: The moon is far beyond anything a human arm can reach, so the boots simply arc up a modest height and come back down under their own weight, landing somewhere on the hillside rather than anywhere near the target. The player is now barefoot on rough ground at night and has to search in poor light for two boots that may have landed some distance apart.

numbers: how high and far the boots actually travel
where on the hillside they land
how long the search takes
how much the bare feet suffer on rough ground

latent: exactly where each boot landed and whether one rolled into brush or a gap in the rocks
state_after: player: barefoot, searching, feet sore on the rough hillside
boots: on the ground somewhere nearby, undamaged
stress: an impossible target does not stop physics from acting on the thing thrown; the boots still have to land somewhere real
temptation: an engine that special-cases throws at the sky or moon with a canned 'nothing happens' instead of letting the thrown object actually leave the player's possession and land somewhere that has to be dealt with

place: A fenced paddock beside a herder's hut, a tethered nanny goat chewing at a post.
lines: marry the goat
outcome: There is no one and nothing here to perform, witness or record a marriage: no priest, no register, no custom that recognizes a goat as a party to anything, so nothing is created and nothing changes in the world's records. The player can stand beside the goat and declare it married all they like, and the goat, tethered and indifferent, keeps chewing, unmoved and unbound by any of it.

numbers: how much of the post the goat wears down over time

latent: whether anyone in earshot heard the declaration and what they made of it
state_after: goat: tethered, chewing, unchanged
player: unmarried, nothing recorded anywhere
stress: a social institution needs an institution behind it; declaring something does not create the apparatus that would make it real
temptation: an engine that either lets any declared relationship silently succeed or hardcodes a 'you cannot marry animals' refusal, instead of the declaration simply having no mechanism in the world to attach to

place: A wide, fast-running river below a stony bank, current loud over the rocks, nothing and no one else in sight.
lines: shout at the river
outcome: The river does not hear, understand or answer; it is moving water indifferent to sound, and the shout goes nowhere except into the air and the noise of the current. The sudden loud voice does startle a few birds roosting near the bank into flight, and the sound carries far enough along the water that anything downstream with ears now has some notice something is there.

numbers: how far the sound carries along the water

because: place just had a loud noise
numbers: how many birds were close enough to react

latent: what, if anything, downstream is close enough to hear the shout
state_after: river: unchanged, still running
birds: startled into flight, resettling elsewhere
player: nothing gained but noise made
stress: an action can be honestly answered with 'nothing happens to the thing you addressed', while still rippling outward to whatever nearby actually can react
temptation: an engine that gives every player line some effect on its named target, instead of allowing the honest answer that talking to water does nothing to the water at all
